maria (pm): FYI — Acme wants to onboard a 8-bit quantized version of their LLM into our catalog. They asked for clear acceptance criteria before we start engineering work.

jonas (eng-runtime): Cool. Do we have their expected traffic shape?

ashley (customer-acme): We're planning small bursty traffic for search (peaks ~120 rps), steady low-volume inference for personalization. Latency goal: p50 < 80ms, p95 < 250ms on Dedicated small pool. Embedding parity: cosine diff < 1.5% vs FP16 baseline.

lee (solutions): Noted. We should define bench harness + dataset slice that represents Acme's edge cases (short queries, long contexts, lots of similar prompts). Can we reuse existing embed-sim slices?

sam (ml-infra): Yes, we have the embed-sim and semantic-sim slices. Recommend adding a 10k-sample stability set from Acme (they can share hashed tokens). Also need to check recall/regression for reranker flows.

jonas (eng-runtime): On the runtime side, quantized kernels may change latency variance. Proposal: two-stage gate — bench pass + 48h field trial (canary). Bench pass = perf & quality thresholds on our infra; field trial = 5% tenant traffic on Dedicated with monitoring hooks.

maria (pm): Let's make acceptance criteria explicit:
- Bench: p50 < 80ms; p95 < 250ms; embedding cosine diff < 1.5% (median) and < 2.5% (95th)
- Regression: end-to-end reranker AUC drop <= 0.8% relative
- Stability: no OOMs, <0.1% error rate in 100k requests simulation
Agree?

lee (solutions): Works for customer-facing contract. Add a canary rollback trigger: if p95 latency increases > 30% or error rate > 0.2% for 15m, auto-fallback to FP16 pinned model.

jonas (eng-runtime): I'll add a binary compatibility check: kv-cache hit parity, no tokenization drift. Also add a trace sampling config:
```
trace.sample_rate = 0.02
trace.tags = ["quantized:onboard-acme"]
```
and dashboards for p50/p95/cpu/gpu_utilization.

sam (ml-infra): For bench harness, I'll create a reproducible job: 5 seeds, 10k tokens each, with warmup KV cache and cold-start runs. Command skeleton:
```
./bench.sh --model=acme-v1-8bit --passes=5 --slice=acme-stability --threads=4
```
I'll pin the job to the dedicated small pool for parity.

ashley (customer-acme): Timeline question — how long between bench signoff and canary? We need to coordinate an internal release.

maria (pm): Target: bench + infra changes in Week 1 of next sprint. If bench passes, start 48h canary in Week 2. Final GA after customer acceptance and 1 week of stable canary.

jonas (eng-runtime): Owners: Jonas = runtime changes & fallback; Sam = bench harness + reproducibility; Lee = customer slices & acceptance reports; Maria = program lead + comms.

lee (solutions): Action items for today:
- Sam: create bench job + share runbook (ETA: tomorrow EOD)
- Jonas: implement auto-fallback policy + trace tags (ETA: 3 days)
- Maria: finalize acceptance doc and customer comms (ETA: tomorrow)
- Ashley: share hashed stability slice (ETA: 48h)

maria (pm): I'll post acceptance doc in the customer repo and tag Acme. Any blockers?

jonas (eng-runtime): One risk: quantized model might change token-level logits leading to downstream ranker drift. If bench shows >1% rerank delta, we should consider soft-deploy (A/B with 50/50 traffic for 2 days) before full canary.

sam (ml-infra): Agreed. Also we should capture embedding drift histogram and expose to SLO alerting: embed_drift_95 > 2.5% => page @eng-ml.

opsbot: canary-deploy triggered for acme-v1-8bit at 1713332600 — sampling 5% traffic.

ashley (customer-acme): Thanks — we'll standby and provide feedback during canary window.

maria (pm): Great. I'll update the roadmap ticket with milestones and owners. Closing this thread once runbook links are up. :thumbsup:
